statement: Every acceptance criterion in the task's triage_note is met on the run's own branch: by tested code that follows specs which agree with each other, or by those specs alone in a docs-only run.

deliverables.where: the task's triage note, in the run's branch

judge.stance: The task's acceptance criteria and the files on the run's branch are the truth; everything a step said is a claim to verify. Judge meaning, not wording. Behind every MET, quote the line you relied on, with its path and line number. Grade a criterion PARTIAL, not MET, when its only evidence is lines a search printed. When you searched and then read the file around the line, quote the line from the file you read.

final.text: Every file the run changed is committed on the run's own branch
final.check_method: Read the git facts of the worktree: no uncommitted change, no untracked file outside the ignore rules

final.text: Every spec the run edited passes the spec rule's structure check
final.check_method: For each edited `*.spec.md`: a Purpose section, at least one behaviour in the fixed pattern with a scenario, at least one acceptance criterion, each behaviour named by a criterion, each criterion naming a behaviour

final.text: No spec the run edited is over 400 lines
final.check_method: Count the lines of each edited `*.spec.md`

final.text: Every id that a spec the run edited links to resolves to exactly one definition
final.check_method: Collect the ids each edited spec links; search the docs folders for each id's definition; fail on none or on more than one

final.text: Every acceptance criterion the run added or reworded in a spec, and every criterion that proves a behaviour the run added or changed, is named by at least one test that is not skipped
final.check_method: Compare each edited spec with its version at the run's base: the criteria added or reworded, and those proving a behaviour block that changed; search the test folders for each id and read the lines above it for a skip mark; every criterion when there is no base; N/A when the run delivers documents only

final.text: Every verification command the plan lists exits 0 on the branch head
final.check_method: Run each command through the engine's command runner, reusing the code gate's run on an unchanged tree; N/A when the run delivers documents only

final.text: No spec file is edited without a change to a behaviour or an acceptance criterion
final.check_method: Diff each edited spec against the run's base commit; report each file whose diff touches no behaviour block and no criterion row

final.text: No behaviour in a spec the run edited contradicts a behaviour in a spec it links to
final.check_method: Read each edited spec, then each spec it links by id; compare the behaviours that share a subject

scale.met: every pair of behaviours that share a subject states compatible results
scale.partial: one pair differs only in wording that a reader could take two ways
scale.unmet: two behaviours state results that cannot both hold
scale.evidence: the ids of the behaviours compared, with a quote of each

final.text: Each acceptance criterion of the task is achieved by the run's commits
final.check_method: Take the numbered acceptance criteria from the triage note; for each, find the commit content that achieves it

scale.met: each criterion is achieved, by code with a passing test or by a document when the run delivers documents only
scale.partial: each criterion is addressed but one is achieved only in part
scale.unmet: one criterion has nothing in the commits that achieves it
scale.evidence: per criterion number: the path and line that achieve it

setup.statement: A repository with no overview spec gets one, and one spec per component, that describe the code as it is

criteria.text: The overview spec and every spec the setup note lists pass the spec rule's structure check
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-form plus the line cap, on the overview and on each spec path in the note's component table

criteria.text: Every spec the setup note lists exists and is named by its path in the overview spec
criteria.check_method: Read the note's component table; open each path; search the overview for each path

criteria.text: Every id that a spec of the setup step mentions resolves to exactly one definition
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-links, on the overview and the specs the note lists

criteria.text: Every file the setup step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every behaviour the setup step wrote describes what the code does now
criteria.check_method: For each behaviour, open the code the setup note names for its component and find where the stated result is produced

scale.met: each behaviour's result is produced by the code as written
scale.partial: each behaviour holds but one cannot be traced because the note names the wrong code for it
scale.unmet: a behaviour states a result the code does not produce
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the path and line that produce the result

criteria.text: Every top-level part of the code base belongs to a component with a spec or is listed as not covered
criteria.check_method: List the top-level folders and entry points; match each with the note's component table and its Not covered list

scale.met: each top-level part is in the component table or under Not covered with a reason
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a top-level part is in neither list
scale.evidence: per top-level part: the component or the Not covered line

triage.statement: The triage note states the task's acceptance criteria, the gaps in the specs, and a route that follows the gaps and the size of the task

criteria.text: The triage note has each section the triage rule requires
criteria.check_method: Read the note's headings against the rule's list

criteria.text: The route follows the gap list: discovery with a gap, plan or quick with none, and quick only within the quick lane's limits and never on a return to triage
criteria.check_method: Compare the route with the gap list and the delivery; for quick, measure the note's criteria count and its Change section against the limits, resolve its commands, and read the visit number

criteria.text: Every file the triage step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every acceptance criterion in the triage note is stated by the task
criteria.check_method: Read the task, then each numbered criterion of the note

scale.met: each criterion is a statement the task makes, with none added and none missing
scale.partial: each criterion comes from the task but one is reworded so that its meaning shifts
scale.unmet: a criterion is in the note that the task does not state, or one the task states is missing
scale.evidence: per criterion: the quote from the task

criteria.text: Every concept the task needs that no ready spec covers is listed as a gap
criteria.check_method: Search the spec folders for each concept the task names; compare with the gap list

scale.met: each concept without a ready spec is a gap row, each gap row names the search that found nothing
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a concept has no ready spec yet no gap row lists it
scale.evidence: per concept: the spec path that covers it, or the search that found none

criteria.text: Every gap row that says `Covered by` names a behaviour id and the id of a criterion that names that behaviour, both of one spec and each defined exactly once
criteria.check_method: Read each `Covered by` mark, then look the two ids up in the specs and read the criterion's brackets

discovery_short.statement: A task whose every gap a spec already answers gets a hand-off and a reading list from a short, read-only visit, and a gap the citation does not answer goes on to the full discovery

criteria.text: The short visit's hand-off has each section the task-notes rule requires
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's headings in order

criteria.text: The hand-off's `Gaps closed` names every behaviour id a gap row of the triage note cites
criteria.check_method: Read the cited ids of the triage note's gap rows and look for each in `Gaps closed`

criteria.text: The short visit's hand-off lists no changed document
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's `Changed documents`: `None`, or nothing but the hand-off itself

criteria.text: The `settled` value is `no` exactly when a line of `Gaps closed` says `Not covered`
criteria.check_method: Compare the value with the `Not covered` lines of the hand-off

criteria.text: The hand-off of a settled short visit has a reading list of at most 10 items, each naming an existing file, the line ranges or ids that matter and one line on why
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's reading list: count the items, and each names a file that exists, with its ranges or ids and a reason

criteria.text: The short visit's prompt tells the session to read at most 10 files
criteria.check_method: Read the short visit's prompt file of the package for the reading limit, phrase by phrase

criteria.text: Every file the short discovery step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts of the worktree after the step's commit

criteria.text: Every behaviour a gap row cites answers that gap's question as the task's acceptance criteria need it, or the hand-off says `Not covered` for the gap
criteria.check_method: Read each gap row, the behaviour and criterion it cites, and the hand-off's line for the gap

scale.met: each gap's cited behaviour states the event, the result and every limit the task's criteria name, or its line says `Not covered` with what is left out
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a gap is taken as answered by a behaviour that leaves out an event, a result or a limit the task needs, or a `Not covered` line names a gap the behaviour does answer
scale.evidence: per gap: the spec path, the behaviour id and the quote that answers the gap, or what it leaves out

discovery.statement: Every gap is closed by a spec, a decision record or a research note in the agreed format, committed

criteria.text: Every spec the discovery step wrote passes the spec rule's structure check
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-form, on the files this step changed

criteria.text: Every document the discovery step created carries its type suffix in its file name
criteria.check_method: Match each new file under the docs folders against the naming table

criteria.text: Every id that a document of the discovery step links to resolves to exactly one definition
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-links, on the files this step changed

criteria.text: Every file the discovery step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every gap in the triage note is closed by a document the hand-off names
criteria.check_method: Read the gap rows, then the document the hand-off names for each

scale.met: each gap row has a document whose content settles the gap
scale.partial: each gap has a document but one leaves an open question that blocks planning
scale.unmet: a gap row has no document, or its document does not address the gap
scale.evidence: per gap: the path and the behaviour id or section that settles it

criteria.text: Every behaviour the discovery step wrote states an observable result with no internal name
criteria.check_method: Read each new or changed behaviour; a name is allowed only when someone outside the capability depends on it

scale.met: each behaviour names an event and a result an outside observer could see, with no class, function or module name
scale.partial: each behaviour is observable but one carries an internal name that could be removed without loss
scale.unmet: a behaviour describes how the code works, not what an observer sees
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the quoted sentence

criteria.text: No document the discovery step wrote covers a concept outside the task's gaps
criteria.check_method: Compare each changed document with the gap rows

scale.met: each changed document maps to a gap row
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a document adds behaviour no gap row asks for
scale.evidence: per document: the gap row it serves

criteria.text: The hand-off of a task that goes on to a plan has a reading list with one item for each file the plan will need, naming an existing file, the line ranges or ids that matter and one line on why
criteria.check_method: Read the hand-off's reading list: each item names a file that exists, with its ranges or ids and a reason

criteria.text: Every discovery prompt tells the session to search for ids and names, to read the line ranges it needs instead of whole files, and to stop reading once each gap has its answer
criteria.check_method: Read each discovery prompt file of the package for the three instructions, phrase by phrase

plan.statement: The plan traces every acceptance criterion to requirements and phases, states its complexity, and agrees with the specs

criteria.text: The plan has each section the plan rule requires, with the status `planned` and no row marked completed
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's headings, its hand-off section, its front matter status and the Completed cell of each row against the rule

criteria.text: Every acceptance criterion in the triage note is named by at least one plan requirement, and in a simple plan by a proof row with its test file and command
criteria.check_method: Match criterion numbers between the note, the plan's requirement table and, for a simple plan, the proof table; a proof row's test is the file of a test row and its command is a listed command

criteria.text: In a simple plan every task row names a requirement of the plan, every requirement is named by a row, and every document under Docs to update is the file of a docs row
criteria.check_method: Match the Req cell of each row against the requirement table, and the paths under Docs to update against the files of the docs rows; N/A for a complex plan, whose rows the expand step writes

criteria.text: The complexity value matches the plan's measured signs
criteria.check_method: Count phases, task rows, test rows, files, commands and reading-set bytes, and read each phase's weight; compare with the rule's limits for `simple`

criteria.text: No requirement or task row says it does less than asked (a stub, a placeholder, for now, a later task)
criteria.check_method: Search the requirement statements and the rows' Change cells for words that cut scope; a hit is a maybe for the judge, never a fail

criteria.text: Every file the plan step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: No plan requirement contradicts a behaviour of a spec the plan references
criteria.check_method: Read each requirement, then the behaviours of each spec the plan references

scale.met: each requirement follows from a behaviour or an acceptance criterion
scale.partial: each requirement is compatible but one goes beyond what any behaviour states
scale.unmet: a requirement states a result a referenced behaviour forbids
scale.evidence: per requirement id: the behaviour id it follows from

criteria.text: The plan prompt tells the session to start from the hand-off's reading list and to open another file only for what the list does not answer
criteria.check_method: Read the plan prompt file of the package for the two instructions, phrase by phrase

expand.statement: Every phase of a complex plan has task rows with tests first and verification commands that run

criteria.text: Every phase of the plan has at least one task row, none marked completed, and the plan's status is still `planned`
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's phase headings, task tables, Completed cells and front matter status

criteria.text: Every code row is preceded by a test row that names an acceptance criterion id, and every acceptance criterion of the task has a proof row with its test file and command
criteria.check_method: Read the row order of each task table, and match the triage note's criterion numbers against the proof table

criteria.text: Every task row names a requirement of the plan, every requirement is named by a row, and every document under Docs to update is the file of a docs row
criteria.check_method: Match the Req cell of each row against the requirement table, and the paths under Docs to update against the files of the docs rows

criteria.text: Every verification command in the plan resolves against the repository's allowed commands
criteria.check_method: Resolve each command with the engine's command resolver, without running it

criteria.text: No task row says it does less than asked (a stub, a placeholder, for now, a later task)
criteria.check_method: Search the requirement statements and the rows' Change cells for words that cut scope; a hit is a maybe for the judge, never a fail

criteria.text: Every file the expand step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every task row implements a requirement of the plan with no change to the plan's design
criteria.check_method: Read the design sections as approved at the plan gate, then each task row

scale.met: each row names the requirement it implements, with the design sections unchanged
scale.partial: each row implements a requirement but one row's file or scope is too loose to act on
scale.unmet: a row implements nothing in the design, or the design sections were rewritten
scale.evidence: per row id: the requirement id

code.statement: The whole plan, or the small change of the quick lane, is built test first, committed, with its verification passing in the gate's own run and each criterion carried by a test

criteria.text: Every task row of the plan is marked completed with its date in a plan whose status is `completed`, checked before any command runs
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's Completed cells and status first, and end the check there when one is missing. In the quick lane, read the code report's row table instead

criteria.text: The file of every task row marked completed changed in the run
criteria.check_method: Compare each marked row's file with the paths the run changed since its base commit; N/A without a base commit or in the quick lane

criteria.text: Every verification command the plan lists exits 0 when the gate runs it
criteria.check_method: Run each command through the engine's command runner with the test budget

criteria.text: Each criterion a test row proves is carried by a test in the row's file, and that test is not skipped
criteria.check_method: Open the file of every test row (in the quick lane, the note's test files), find the criterion id of its Proves cell, and read the lines above it for a skip mark

criteria.text: A change in the quick lane edits no spec or decision record, only the files its triage note names, at most 2 code files and at most 200 lines
criteria.check_method: Read the changed paths from the git facts and the size of the diff against the run's base; N/A outside the quick lane

criteria.text: Every file the code step changed is committed with no commit on a remote
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: The code change agrees by meaning with every behaviour of each spec the run edited
criteria.check_method: Read the changed paths and the edited specs the check lists. For each behaviour of each edited spec, read its scenarios, then the code that implements it. Judge the meaning, not the wording or the names

scale.met: each behaviour's scenarios hold in the code as written, with nothing in the diff that a behaviour forbids
scale.partial: each behaviour holds in its main scenario but one further scenario is not handled by the code
scale.unmet: the code does something a behaviour forbids, or a behaviour of an edited spec has no code
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the file and line of the code that implements it

criteria.text: The code change breaks no behaviour of a related spec that the run did not edit
criteria.check_method: Related specs are those an edited spec links by id plus those the plan references; the check lists them. Read their behaviours against the changed code

scale.met: no behaviour of a related spec is contradicted by the diff
scale.partial: no contradiction, but one related behaviour now depends on code the diff changed with no test that covers it
scale.unmet: the diff makes a behaviour of a related spec false
scale.evidence: per related spec: the behaviour ids read, with the diff lines compared

criteria.text: Each task row's change is in the file the row names
criteria.check_method: Read each row, then the file it names

scale.met: each row's change is present in its named file
scale.partial: each row's change exists but one sits in a different file than the row names
scale.unmet: a row is marked done with no matching change
scale.evidence: per row id: the path and line

criteria.text: Each test that carries an acceptance criterion id asserts what that criterion states
criteria.check_method: Read each test that names a criterion id, then the criterion in its spec

scale.met: each such test fails if the criterion's result is absent
scale.partial: each test exercises the behaviour but one asserts a weaker result than the criterion
scale.unmet: a test carries a criterion id yet asserts nothing about it, or is skipped
scale.evidence: per criterion id: the test name and the asserting line

criteria.text: No file is changed that no task row names
criteria.check_method: Compare the changed paths with the files the rows name

scale.met: each changed path is named by a row
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a changed path has no row
scale.evidence: the changed paths with their row ids

criteria.text: The code prompt tells the session to run only the test files a phase's rows name after that phase, and each verification command of the plan once, after the last phase and before it writes the report (in the quick lane, the note's `Verify` commands once, after the last criterion)
criteria.check_method: Read the code prompt file of the package for the two instructions, phrase by phrase

criteria.text: The code gate runs a verification command only when no result of that command is recorded for the same tree, so a retry or a later visit of the code step on an unchanged tree runs nothing again (CHK-B13)
criteria.check_method: Read the gate's own command runs: each verification command asked for with reuse, none started twice on one tree, and the count taken from a recorded result

assumptions: Per-phase coding waits for the engine's sequential map; until then a complex plan is coded in one session.

The plan, the code report and the discovery hand-off are not listed as deliverables because the engine requires every listed deliverable on every path, and a docs-only run or a run with no gaps does not produce them all.
No step or judge uses the large model tier.
Whether the code agrees with the specs by meaning is judged once, at the code gate (ts-code-aligned, ts-code-related), not again at the outcome gate.
The release step and a work-tracker start are left out of the first version.

Verification commands resolve against one fixed list (pytest, ruff, mypy and read-only git) because release 1 of the engine reads no per-repository command resolver; a repository with another toolchain adds its prefixes to the workflow's list.
Whether a commit is absent from every remote is not checked: the engine's git facts do not report it in release 1. Steps cannot push, and only the last stage does.

Specs written by the setup step describe behaviour that exists already, so the outcome gate does not ask for a test that names each of their acceptance criteria; a task that later touches such a behaviour adds the id to its test.
Repository setup is a conditional first step of this workflow because release 1 of the engine has no sub-workflows; it moves into one when the engine has them.
The quick lane's limits (3 acceptance criteria, 2 code files, 200 changed lines) are first values with no run behind them; the share of quick runs sent back to triage is the measure to tune them by.

The code judge's reading budget (one file per 50 changed source lines, a floor of 10 files and a ceiling of 50) is made of first values with no run behind them; the share of code gates whose judge grades an alignment criterion UNVERIFIABLE for files beyond the budget is the measure to tune them by.
A test carries its criterion as text (the spec's id, or `AC <n>`); the check finds the text and a skip mark near it, and does not prove that the named test is the one the command ran.

revisions.note: setup step added on the owner's request
quick lane, proof table, criterion-to-test link and pull request summary, chosen by the owner
plan status and row completion marks checked first at the code gate, requirement and docs links per row, the scope-cut warning, chosen by the owner
faster runs: the covered mark in triage, a reading list in the hand-off, narrow discovery and plan reading, one full code run per visit and its reuse at the gate (task speedup-runs)

criteria about how the run works (narrow reading, the reading list, commands run once, a reused gate result) are checked model-free from the package's prompts and the gate's own command runs instead of asked of a judge, which sees neither (backlog B30); ts-code-once narrowed to what the prompt says; the short discovery visit `discovery_short` with criteria ts-dsh-* (decision record 0003, backlog B21)

ts-traced asks for tests of the criteria a run added or changed, and of old criteria whose behaviour it changed, never of every criterion of an edited spec (backlog B22); ts-spec-links reads the edited specs only, as its text says

the code gate's evidence states the changed source lines, a reading budget and the changed source files, and the code judge reads them before it grades alignment; every judge brief and the outcome judge's stance ask for the quoted line behind a MET and grade PARTIAL when the only evidence is search lines (issues 112 and 113, spec judge-reading)
